summary: I re-priced the ladder on the official Treasury curve up to the 15 Oct close. The room under $300k has collapsed. On the IBTR note's own basis (WInS-listed maturities, yields unchanged) the ten payments now cost $298,624. That leaves $1,376, or 4.7bp; on 6 Oct the room was 22.7bp. A rough model puts the chance that the ladder costs more than $300k by January at about 45%. So the IBTR note's "about 0.2 points", the planned reflection's "yields have fallen slightly", V5's "$292,000" and COMPETITION.md's "$293k / 0.2pp" are all stale. The 2028 top-up is now a central case, and under V5's own "remainder" rule a top-up shrinks the floor. The same re-pricing cuts the plan's stock share from about 9% (about $40k) to about 7.2% (about $33.5k). WInS holds 8.8% VT, and COMPETITION.md calls the drift "trivial" because it measures against fixed 6 Oct targets. The VT note, which cannot be edited, says stocks "only" set the gift above the minimum. V5 gives Laura's half of the fund three more jobs: covering payment shortfalls, defending against inflation and a stronger Taiwan dollar, and acting as a cushion. That half is worth only about $23k by 2033 (MODEL), and the 2027 leftover that comes first is about $1.4k and sits in stocks. The floor has six definitions across team files. The team's own rab memo rejects quoting $150k because the IBTM floor "pays under $150,000 about 2 times in 3", yet $150k is still the figure in most team files. V5's "never below the floor" survives only because the floor used to be STRIPS: the journal says so, and the 6 Oct email removed that reason. Other gaps: the WInS book is the 2 Jan 2028 plan scaled by about 0.643, but 9 of 11 notes speak of "$50,000 payments" with no scale. V5 says payments depend "mainly on the US government", while the notes admit reinvestment and payout risk; coupons supply 38-44% of each bond-funded payment. The reserve size is never defined (old files say $413k, $422k or $500k; the 15 Oct curve gives about $396-405k). One correction to the 15 Oct brief: "$292k" also reproduces on the WInS-listed forward basis for 29-30 Sep, so the real defect is a missing date and basis label, not only the old STRIPS basis. The fixes all need one dated numbers sheet with a re-price rule (6 Nov close for the IPS and Final Report), one glossary, and votes on the floor, the shortfall order and what the WInS mirror is pinned to.
